html:
A Mandinka kingdom centred on Kansala in what is now eastern Guinea-Bissau, first a western province of the Mali Empire and independent after Mali declined in the 16th century.

Its warrior nobility, the nyancho, ruled many peoples between the Gambia and Geba rivers. Kaabu grew rich by raiding for captives and selling them to the Portuguese at ports such as Cacheu, and it was among the main suppliers of the Atlantic slave trade on this coast. In the 19th century the Fula of Futa Jallon attacked it, and it fell at the siege of Kansala in 1867. Its memory lives in Mandinka oral epics.
sum: A Mandinka kingdom centred on Kansala in what is now eastern Guinea-Bissau, first a western province of the Mali Empire and independent after Mali declined in the 16th century.
